links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of original vs chatbot-simplified pathology reports
links.effect: Grade level fell from 13.19 to 8.17 (chatbot 1) and 7.45 (chatbot 2); Flesch Reading Ease rose from 10.32 to 61.32 and 70.80 (all P<.001).
links.quote: For the 1134 reports included, the Flesch-Kincaid grade level decreased from a mean of 13.19 (95% CI, 12.98-13.41) to 8.17 (95% CI, 8.08-8.25; t = 45.29; P < .001) by chatbot 1 and 7.45 (95% CI, 7.35-7.54; t = 49.69; P < .001) by chatbot 2.

links.outcome: Medical correctness and hallucinations in chatbot-simplified pathology reports
links.effect: Chatbot 1: 87.57% correct, 8.99% partially correct, 3.44% incorrect, 32 hallucinations (2.82%). Chatbot 2: 97.44% correct, 0.44% incorrect, 3 hallucinations (0.26%).
links.quote: Chatbot 1 had 32 instances of hallucinations (2.82%), while chatbot 2 had 3 (0.26%).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the baseline accuracy, readability, and hallucination rates of two commercial LLMs (Bard and GPT-4) when simplifying pathology reports for patients, but does not compare outcomes with versus without a specific safeguard or deployment practice.
